title: Applicability-domain-constrained prediction of landfill-relevant odor descriptors using integrated chemical knowledge
abstract: Malodor emissions from municipal solid waste treatment facilities are complex environmental exposure mixtures, making rapid identification of odor-relevant compounds difficult using olfactometry or compound-by-compound GC-MS interpretation. Here, we developed a knowledge-guided molecular learning framework for interpretable and reliability-aware prediction of waste-treatment malodors. The framework integrates Morgan fingerprints, large language model-derived structure-odor rules, deterministic functional-group descriptors, and StructKG-derived hierarchical structural semantics. On a curated dataset of 3756 molecules, the fused representation with XGBoost achieved the best performance, with an AU-PRC of 0.437 and an AU-ROC of 0.869. To improve transferability to external chemical space, we introduced a multi-label applicability domain combining local similarity density with neighborhood label inconsistency, increasing in-domain AU-PRC to 0.545. External validation using compounds detected at the Shanghai Laogang waste-treatment site showed that malodor-related predictions increased from 66% outside the domain to 93% inside it. Model interpretation and theoretical odor concentration-weighted attribution identified reduced sulfur compounds, amines, volatile fatty acids, and reactive carbonyls as major odor-marker classes, supporting targeted monitoring and control of waste-treatment malodors.

title: Deciphering foliar uptake mechanisms of organophosphate esters in plant leaves: Molecular structure–cuticular wax interactions revealed by experimental evidence and machine learning
abstract: The foliar uptake and inward penetration mechanisms of organophosphate esters (OPEs) in plant leaves from agricultural systems remain unclear. This study systematically investigated OPE foliar uptake on excised leaves from nine plant species (crops and ornamental woody plants). Aryl-OPEs exhibited rapid initial absorption (uptake rate constant of pseudo-first-order kinetics, k = 0.35-1.45 h⁻¹), whereas Cl-OPEs showed higher final accumulation (0.07-0.38 nmol per 25 cm²). Machine learning analysis using tree-based models (GBRT/RF) models under compound-grouped nested cross-validation highlighted that polymethyl-structure promoted initial partitioning of OPEs into cuticular wax but limited intra-leaf inward penetration. Additionally, P-OH groups (e.g., diester transformation products of OPEs) facilitated transport within leaves, while side-chain hydroxyl groups reduced uptake and inward penetration. Cuticular wax composition also modulated uptake: alkenes enhanced aryl-OPE absorption via π-electron-mediated dispersion interactions, whereas phytosterols and fatty acids exerted inhibitory effects on total accumulation and inward transfer, likely through polar hydrogen-bonding interactions. For inward penetration specifically, diterpenoids facilitated OPE transfer from the wax layer into inner tissues. These findings provide an integrated mechanistic framework for OPE foliar uptake, offering mechanistic insights into cuticular barrier function that are relevant to plant exposure in agricultural environments.

title: A contaminant-adaptive evidence chain for source attribution in multi-operator contaminated land
abstract: Source attribution is difficult when successive on-site operations overlap and candidate sources occur beyond parcel boundaries. We developed a contaminant-adaptive evidence chain and applied it to 307 soil records from 72 locations at an electroplating-to-recycling site. Risk screening under future sensitive land use prioritized Cr(VI), total Cr, Ni, Zn, Pb and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH), while Cu provided a strongly reconstructed processing fingerprint. Process and material-use histories, correlation, principal component analysis (PCA), and positive matrix factorization (PMF) resolved Cu, Zn and total Cr as electroplating-associated signals; Cr(VI) was co-interpreted with total Cr as a redox-specific fraction. Pb and TPH remained multi-source candidates spanning the internal electroplating-recycling overlap and adjacent enterprises. For these residuals, internal maxima and distance-decay, runoff, groundwater-gradient and pipeline-connectivity evidence reduced the plausibility of evaluated off-site inputs. Within the parcel, performance-gated machine learning with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) bounded diffuse TPH to the internal overlap, whereas unstable Pb prediction routed Pb to HYDRUS-1D transport testing. Near-surface Pb was compatible with at least one tested surface-input matrix-transport history, whereas deep Pb and the SA20 TPH maximum were not reproduced by the tested one-dimensional histories and were localized for verification. By turning routine investigation data into a bounded attribution hierarchy, the framework resolves coherent source domains, separates competing evidence tracks and identifies where targeted confirmation and forensic evidence collection are required.

title: Native-state monitoring of nanoplastic corona dynamics and their mitigating role in ecotoxicity using an integrated hollow fiber flow field-flow fractionation platform
abstract: Upon entering environmental systems, nanoplastics (NPs) adsorb natural organic matter, forming eco-coronas that dictate their ecotoxicological fate. However, conventional isolation alters fragile corona structures, and unseparated free biomolecules confound toxicity assessments, making native-state characterization challenging. To overcome this, we developed an integrated platform coupling hollow fiber flow field-flow fractionation with UV-Vis and point-discharge optical emission spectrometry (HF5-UV/PD-OES). This gentle separation isolated intact corona-coated polystyrene NPs (PSNPs) while eliminating free-molecule interference. Tracking native-state temporal dynamics of bovine serum albumin (BSA) and fulvic acid (FA) coronas revealed a three-stage evolution: rapid adsorption, structural reorganization, and dynamic equilibrium. Governed by surface curvature, 100 nm PSNPs accommodated significantly thicker coronas than highly curved 50 nm counterparts. A hybrid CNN-BiLSTM deep-learning model decoded PD-OES spectral fingerprints, accurately discriminating pristine, BSA-coated, and FA-coated PSNPs (98.67% accuracy). Using these highly purified fractions, ecotoxicological assays on Tetrahymena thermophila provided unconfounded evidence that the corona acts as a protective interfacial shield. While effectively mitigating acute oxidative stress and lethality, internalized particles continue to impose a persistent sub-lethal physical burden on cells. This study offers a robust tool for probing NP surface transformations and proves the corona decisively modulates toxicity in ecological risk assessments.

title: The construction of UiO-66(Ce)/Cu oxidase for multivariate identification of acetylcholinesterase, organophosphorus pesticides and tannic acid supported by machine learning
abstract: The widespread abuse of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) threatens human health and ecological sustainability. The development of a portable, intelligent, and prompt detection strategy poses a key priority in both environment and human health, but remains a significant challenge. Here, visual detection of OPs was achieved based on its inhibition of acetylcholinesterase (AChE), using the constructed metal-organic framework (MOF) composite UiO-66(Ce)/Cu as a catalyst in the 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) oxidation process. The coexistence of Cu 2 + /Cu + and Ce 4+ /Ce 3+ redox pairs synergistically promoted electron transfer and oxidase-mimicking (OXD-mimicking) catalysis. Based on the oxidation capability of UiO-66(Ce)/Cu and reversible colorimetric response, the AChE, OPs, and tannic acid (TA) can be detected assisted by the smartphone integrating with the machine learning algorithm. The limits of detection for TA, AChE, and OPs were determined to be 0.344 μM, 0.102 mU mL⁻¹ , and 0.0891 μg mL⁻¹ , respectively. In addition, satisfactory recoveries of 91.95-106.04% were obtained from real water and food samples, further corroborating the applicability of the intelligent and visual readout system for the portable analysis of OPs and TA. This work presented a practical strategy for constructing MOF-based OXD-mimicking nanozyme toward cascade biosensing and food safety applications.

title: Machine learning-assisted ratiometric Zr-MOF-based fluorescent probe for intelligent detection of uranyl ions
abstract: Uranium contamination in aquatic environments poses potential threats to ecosystems and human health due to the high radioactive and chemical toxicity of uranyl ions (UO 2 2 + ), necessitating the development of accurate and rapid detection strategies for the monitoring of UO 2 2+ . Herein, a zirconium-based metal-organic framework (NH 2 -PCN-134) was constructed through a one-pot hydrothermal method and employed as a ratiometric fluorescent probe for the detection of UO 2 2+ . The ratiometric fluorescence response of NH 2 -PCN-134 toward UO 2 2+ featured emission quenching at 655 nm and enhancement at 515 nm, enabling quantitative analysis based on the I 515 /I 655 intensity ratio. Furthermore, the probe exhibited a broad linear response range of 0-200 μM with a low detection limit of 1.23 μM, and excellent selectivity toward UO 2 2+ in the presence of various interfering ions. The ratiometric fluorescence response was attributed to the synergistic effects of photoinduced electron transfer (PET) and molecular interactions between NH 2 -PCN-134 and UO 2 2+ . Moreover, the color features extracted from fluorescent images were integrated with multiple machine learning models for quantitative prediction, which exhibited strong agreement between the predicted and experimental values even in the presence of interfering ions, demonstrating their effectiveness for quantitative analysis. This study provides a machine learning-assisted ratiometric fluorescence sensing strategy for intelligent detection of UO 2 2+ , highlighting its potential for environmental monitoring.

title: Biogenic maturation of mineral-encrusted plastispheres overrides ecological drift to orchestrate multi-kingdom assembly and nitrogen reprogramming in agroecosystems
abstract: The quantitative assembly rules and multi-kingdom functional gateways of the soil plastisphere remain poorly resolved. We integrated multi-omics with high-resolution surface deconvolution to decode the ecological signatures of weathered polyethylene (PE) films in intensive agroecosystems. Surface characterization revealed an interfacial metamorphosis where biogenic maturation facilitated the formation of a dense mineral organic crust, transforming inert polymers into reactive metabolic islands. Ecological modeling identifies a distinct departure from neutral assembly, demonstrating that niche-based selection driven by polymer surface remodeling overrides ecological drift in shaping microbial consortia. Machine learning and structural equation modeling identify ammonia oxidizing archaea as the primary functional keystone taxa orchestrating the global interactome. This archaeal-bacterial axis, regulated by protistan assemblages that exhibit significant topological densification, catalyzes a cross-kingdom metabolic relay synchronized with nitrogenous biomarker accumulation and intensified enzymatic mineralization. Functional decoupling across taxonomic domains reveals a metabolic lag where rapid deterministic recruitment outpaces steady-state nutrient stabilization. While promoting local alpha-diversity, the bacterial core exhibits structural fragmentation and elevated antagonistic interactions, signaling an asynchronous regime shift that may trigger positive priming effects on native soil organic carbon. These findings establish a mechanistic blueprint for how weathered PE residues redirect terrestrial nutrient fluxes via deterministic multi-kingdom assembly, pinpointing specific organo-mineral signatures and archaeal keystone taxa as critical targets for precision microbiome engineering in the Anthropocene.

title: Microbial necromass carbon links soil carbon sequestration to heavy metal stabilization under long-term fertilization
abstract: Long-term fertilization sustains soil productivity but concurrently introduces heavy metals (HMs) into agroecosystems. The mechanisms by which soil carbon pools regulate HM speciation, however, remain inadequately understood. Based on a 15-year field experiment, this study investigated the influence of fertilization on HM accumulation and speciation in relation to microbial necromass carbon (MNC), soil aggregation, and microbial community reorganization. Fertilization increased soil carbon pools, soil organic carbon increased by 44% under mineral fertilization and by 101-140% under organic amendments, while MNC rose by 92% and 304-342%, respectively. Sequential extraction revealed a consistent redistribution of HMs toward oxidizable fractions, particularly under organic fertilization where the proportion of this fraction increased by 7-26% relative to the unfertilized control. Shifts in microbial community composition toward copiotrophic taxa accelerated microbial turnover and promoted necromass accumulation. Aggregate-scale analyses further demonstrated that MNC was preferentially enriched in macroaggregates > 0.25 mm, whereas HMs were preferentially enriched in the 0.25-2 mm fraction. Random forest highlighted MNC as a primary predictor of Cu and Cd partitioning, whereas PLS-PM indicated that necromass accumulation and direct HM inputs jointly regulate HM speciation. These findings identify MNC as a previously underappreciated biogeochemical interface linking soil carbon stabilization with long-term HM retention in fertilized agricultural soils.

title: vToxiNet: An interpretable deep learning framework for hepatotoxicity prediction and mechanism exploration
abstract: Hepatotoxicity remains a leading cause of drug attrition and post-marketing withdrawal, resulting from diverse and complex toxicity mechanisms. Traditional in vitro models can only capture a limited subset of toxicity pathways, and animal studies face translational and ethical limitations. Regulatory agencies have therefore promoted new approach methodologies, including human-relevant assays, omics technologies, and computational models to improve predictive toxicology and support evidence-based decision-making. However, most machine learning models for hepatotoxicity either rely solely on chemical structure or operate as black boxes, limiting mechanistic interpretability and broader applicability. Here, we introduce the virtual toxicity network (vToxiNet), a biologically constrained deep learning framework that embeds systems toxicology knowledge directly into neural network architecture for interpretable hepatotoxicity prediction. vToxiNet integrates chemical descriptors, high-throughput assay responses, transcriptomic signatures, and Reactome pathway hierarchy to construct a virtual adverse outcome pathway network. Across cross-validation and external validation, vToxiNet demonstrates promising predictive performance. Importantly, interpretation of vToxiNet enables gene and pathway-level attribution, supporting mechanism-informed hazard characterization and chemical prioritization. By integrating multimodal data and biological hierarchy as architectural constraints, this study provides a framework that combines prediction with mechanistic interpretation and supports further development of mechanism-informed approaches for chemical hazard assessment.

title: Viral regulation of N2O emissions depends on soil acidity
abstract: Acidification generally enhances N 2 O emissions from soils. Yet, the adaptive responses of denitrifiers and the regulatory roles of soil viruses in denitrifier-mediated N 2 O emissions under persistent acidity remain poorly understood. Here, we combined D 2 O-labeled single-cell Raman spectroscopy, 15 N tracing, metagenomics, machine learning, and virus-addition experiments to examine virus-denitrifier interactions across soils with contrasting long-term acidity conditions maintained for > 17 years. Acidic soils showed the highest N 2 O emissions despite the lowest potential denitrification rate and highest microbial anabolic activity. Denitrifiers and viral populations in acidic soils exhibited reduced microdiversity, stronger purifying selection, and distinct functional specialization, while viruses showed a lower virulent-to-temperate ratio and greater genetic potential for host interaction and persistence. Host antiviral defense capacity was the strongest genomic predictor of abundance responses to active virus. In acidic soils, active viruses increased N 2 O reductase level by 33.2% without altering nosZ abundance and reduced N 2 O accumulation by up to 62.5%, indicating an efficiency-optimized response. Neutral soils showed a quantity-driven response, whereas alkaline soils showed no significant reduction in N 2 O accumulation. These findings reveal acidity-dependent viral regulation of N 2 O emissions, strongest in long-term acidic soils.

title: Machine learning-driven high-throughput prediction of Hg0 capture in MOFs and decipherment of structure-property relationships
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) show potential for Hg 0 adsorption via tunable pore structures and chemical functionalities. However, efficient screening of MOF adsorbents remains challenging due to vast material space and unclear structure-property relationships. Herein, a Hg 0 adsorption database of 6528 MOF samples was established, and machine learning models were developed for predicting adsorption performance. Among tested models, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) exhibited the best prediction on the independent test set, achieving a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.893. SHAP analysis revealed that energy descriptors, including logarithmic Henry coefficient (log(K H )) and adsorption enthalpy (ΔH ads ), dominated Hg 0 adsorption, while structural descriptors further regulated adsorption behavior. Combined model interpretation revealed a condition-dependent interaction between adsorption affinity and pore characteristics. High-throughput screening revealed characteristic descriptor intervals for high-performing MOFs, including log(K H )=-3.62 to -2.61, ΔH ads = -34.60 to -25.21 kJ·mol -1 , and VF = 0.67-0.78. MOFid-based structural analysis identified significant enrichment of Cr, Fe, Co nodes and nbo topology, alongside preferred acs and tbo topologies, as well as nitrogen-containing aromatic conjugated heterocyclic ligands in high-performing MOFs. These findings clarify the roles of metal nodes, topology, and ligand chemistry in Hg 0 adsorption and provide a machine learning-driven strategy for rational design of MOF-based mercury removal adsorbents.

title: HumanToxPredict: An interpretable data-driven framework for human oral TDLo prediction and toxicity assessment of pharmaceuticals and bioactive compounds
abstract: Predicting the human toxic dose low (TDLo) is critically important for pharmaceutical safety assessment and regulatory toxicology. A global computational toxicology framework that integrates toxicity data for children, infants, men, and women was developed using indicator-variable-based demographic encoding. Initially, Partial Least Squares (PLS)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) and quantitative read-across structure-activity relationship (q-RASAR) models were developed using interpretable molecular descriptors and similarity-based descriptors. A structure-level group-wise partitioning strategy was adopted. The q-RASAR model demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with the corresponding QSAR model. Additionally, Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models were explored to investigate non-linear relationships. To further improve practical applicability, classification models were also developed, with RF showing the strongest overall performance among the evaluated models based on multi-metric analysis. Model interpretation suggests that pTDLo values are influenced by substituted nitrogen environments, topological arrangements, and similarity-driven toxicological information. The final model was further applied to 3660 investigational drugs, with most compounds falling within the applicability domain. We also developed a user-friendly software tool, HumanToxPredict, to enable rapid toxicity prediction. Overall, the present study introduces an interpretable, population-integrated human toxicity prediction framework that integrates q-RASAR, machine learning, and large-scale chemical screening.

title: Interpretable QSPR modeling of PFAS endpoints via transformer-driven SMILES-to-molecular descriptor learning
abstract: A data-centric and interpretable Quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) framework was developed for four Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) endpoints (i.e., LC 50 , log BCF, log K OA , and log K OW ) with molecular- and descriptor-level interpretation of prediction behavior. First, PFAS endpoint datasets were collected while molecular descriptors and tokenized SMILES sequences were integrated for descriptor imputation. Descriptor redundancy was then reduced through statistical feature selection, and MissTransformer reconstructed missing descriptor values from latent structural information encoded in SMILES. Finally, explainable AI (XAI) analysis was applied to interpret chemical descriptor contributions to PFAS endpoint prediction. As a result, MissTransformer increased the number of descriptor-complete compounds available for QSPR modeling by 133.71% for log BCF data. Among the endpoint prediction models, the data-centric XGB model showed the best performance for log K OW prediction, with R 2 and Q 2 LMO values of 0.976 and 0.775, respectively. Interpretation results showed that hydrophobicity-related descriptors and fluorine atoms strongly contributed to log K OW prediction, whereas global structural descriptors related to molecular size and steric effects were important for log BCF prediction. The proposed framework can be used to prioritize data-poor PFAS compounds for further testing, monitoring, and risk-based environmental management.

title: Thiamphenicol decouples acidogenesis from methanogenesis and redirects carbon flux toward volatile fatty acids in sludge anaerobic digestion
abstract: Antibiotic residues in waste activated sludge (WAS) may disrupt anaerobic carbon conversion, yet how phenicol antibiotics redistribute carbon between acidogenesis and methanogenesis remains unclear. At 10 mg/g TSS, methane production decreased by 63.2% while VFAs reached 131-fold the control. This functional decoupling was underpinned by microbial fates: hydrolytic-acidogenic bacteria were largely retained or enriched, whereas methanogenic archaea and syntrophic bacteria were severely depleted. Concurrently, bacteria-archaea ecological networks underwent reorganization, with positive correlations partially rebounding at moderate TAP exposure. The network collapsed at high TAP, with substantial loss of connector taxa mediating inter-module metabolite exchange. Metagenomic evidence further revealed a functional asymmetry: genes involved in substrate transport and amino acid metabolism were maintained or showed increased relative abundance, while methanogenic genes and AI-2-associated communication genes exhibited decreased relative abundance. PLS-PM revealed that TAP was positively associated with the acidogenic bacterial community (β = 0.960) but negatively with methanogenic potential (β = -0.998). Accordingly, the methane share dropped from 98.7% to 18.1%, while VFAs increased to 81.9% of the COD-equivalent product pool. This work advances the understanding of antibiotic-driven functional imbalance and carbon flux redirection in sludge anaerobic digestion, providing a mechanistic basis for managing antibiotic-laden sludge prior to energy recovery.

title: Agricultural impacts reshape the distribution and future potential health risks of soil heavy metals across global wheat-growing regions under interactive climate–socioeconomic influences
abstract: Soil heavy metal(loid) pollution poses a critical threat to ecosystem health and sustainability. However, it remains unclear whether agricultural activities have systematically altered their distribution across global wheat-growing regions. Here, we collected paired soil samples from cropland and adjacent non-cropland sites across global wheat-growing regions on six continents to evaluate concentration differences and potential drivers for six heavy metal(loid)s-arsenic (As), nickel (Ni), cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), antimony (Sb), and chromium (Cr). We found clear element-specific patterns: Ni was enriched in high-input agricultural regions, whereas Pb and Cr were more concentrated in non-croplands. These differences varied by region. Using extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), we identified fertilization intensity, moisture conditions, and socioeconomic development as key nonlinear predictors. Projections under the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios suggest that by 2100, these concentration differences may either reverse or intensify, with their spatial evolution accompanied by shifts in potential non-carcinogenic health across cropland soils. Our findings show that agricultural land use is closely associated with spatial patterns of soil heavy metals across global wheat-growing regions and highlight land-use differentials as valuable early indicators of pollution risk, particularly in major wheat-producing regions.

title: Spatial distribution and microbial degradation potential of microplastics and nanoplastics along a 134-year proglacial chronosequence
abstract: Glacier retreat increasingly exposes proglacial soils to micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) pollution, yet long-term MNP dynamics and associated microbial plastic-degradation potential remain unclear. Along a 134-year chronosequence at Hailuogou Glacier, we combined µ-FTIR, Py-GC/MS, and metagenomics to characterize MNP pollution, ecological risk, and microbial degradation potential. MP abundance followed a non-linear trajectory, peaking at 270 items kg⁻¹ at 66 yr, whereas NP abundance increased from 1.54 to 4.17 mg kg⁻¹ . MPs were dominated by PA, PE, PET, and Rayon, while NPs shifted from PMMA to PE dominance (>78%) in mature soils. Ecological risk was non-monotonic and polymer-dependent: MP-associated PERI reached Level IV at 66 yr, whereas NP-associated PERI peaked at 94 yr despite increasing NP mass. This decoupling suggested that risk was strongly influenced by polymer-composition turnover rather than abundance or mass alone. Gene-based microbial plastic-degradation potential increased during succession through enrichment of plastic-degradation-related genes. PLS-PM identified a sequence of positive associations linking glacier retreat age, soil development, MNP pollution, and microbial plastic-degradation potential. Random Forest analysis further highlighted retreat age and Ca among the leading predictors of degradation-gene abundance. These findings provide insights into MNP risk and gene-based microbial plastic-degradation potential in rapidly deglaciating high-altitude ecosystems.

title: Microplastics amplify Cr(VI)-mediated RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer through coupled interfacial, oxidative, and metabolic regulation
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) can accumulate heavy metals and influence plasmid-mediated antibiotic resistance gene (ARGs) transfer, yet the regulatory mechanisms under metal-associated MP exposure remain poorly understood. Here, a polystyrene microplastic-Cr(VI) composite (PSMPs@Cr) was established to investigate RP4 plasmid conjugative transfer by integrating physicochemical characterization, physiological measurements, transcriptomic analysis, and multivariable modeling. PSMPs@Cr exhibited a non-monotonic effect on conjugative transfer, with the highest conjugative transfer frequency (9.4 × 10 -2 ) observed at 20 ppm Cr loading, representing a 4.75-fold increase compared with the control. Cr adsorption reconstructed the MP interface by modifying surface charge, wettability, morphology, and colloidal stability, which was accompanied by altered bacterial adhesion behavior. Meanwhile, PSMPs@Cr exposure induced coordinated changes in ROS accumulation, antioxidant responses, ATP production, membrane-associated functions, and energy metabolism. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed treatment-dependent regulation of oxidative stress, membrane transport, cellular communication, and metabolic pathways. Random forest-SHAP analysis identified zeta potential, CAT activity, ATP, and ROS as relatively important variables associated with CTF variation. Overall, PSMPs@Cr-associated ARGs transfer was linked to coupled interfacial, redox, and energetic processes rather than a single regulatory pathway, providing new insights into how microplastic-metal interactions influence plasmid-mediated horizontal gene transfer under complex contaminant exposure scenarios.

title: National-scale evaluation of groundwater fluoride in Ethiopia using spatially buffered machine learning
abstract: Excess groundwater fluoride (F⁻) is a public health concern in the East African Rift, yet sparse, clustered observations limit reliable national inference. This study developed a leakage-controlled framework to classify groundwater fluoride exceedance above the WHO guideline of 1.5 mg/L, separating well-level prediction from national spatial transferability. A dataset of 1567 observations, including 567 exceedances, was evaluated using five-fold buffered spatial cross-validation with a 75-km train-test exclusion radius. The hydrochemical Extra Trees model (HYD_ET) achieved the strongest well-level performance, with Macro-F1 = 0.830, balanced accuracy = 0.817, MCC = 0.671, ROC-AUC = 0.910, PR-AUC = 0.859, and Brier score = 0.116. In contrast, the environmental-only Random Forest showed negligible geographic transferability (Macro-F1 = 0.495; balanced accuracy = 0.501), while Gaussian indicator kriging achieved Macro-F1 = 0.594. Applicability-domain analysis identified 8.23% of observations outside the model domain. Because no continuous model demonstrated adequate transferability, no wall-to-wall national F⁻-risk surface was retained. Instead, 48.43%, 18.84%, and 32.73% of 10-km grid cells had stronger, moderate, and weaker monitoring support, respectively. This evaluation spans heterogeneous hydrogeological and environmental settings under uneven monitoring across Ethiopia. The results show that strong well-level prediction does not imply reliable national extrapolation and supports groundwater monitoring and data collection.

title: Influence of material properties and environmental factors on VOC emission characteristics from automotive paint sludge
abstract: Automotive paint sludge is a hazardous waste with significant volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions. Effective source control requires understanding how material properties and environmental factors govern key mass-transfer parameters: initial emittable concentration (C m,0 ), diffusion coefficient (D m ), and partition coefficient (K m ). This study couples a finite diffusion model and nonlinear optimization with chamber experiments on oil-based paint sludge to evaluate effects of temperature, humidity, air exchange rate, VOC type, porosity, moisture, and solid matrix. Temperature dominates: increasing temperature raises C m,0 and D m but lowers K m , and correlating K m with temperature yields apparent desorption activation energies (E d ). Although relative humidity induces minor non-monotonic fluctuations via competitive water adsorption and air exchange rate slightly alters surface convection, their standardized sensitivities are two orders of magnitude below temperature's, rendering their net impacts engineering-wise negligible. Low-molecular-weight, nonpolar VOCs have low E d and desorb rapidly, whereas hydrogen bonding hinders polar alcohols. D m increases with porosity via a power law, suggesting compaction for mitigation. Moisture forms water films that reduce C m,0 and D m but increase K m , and inorganic scaffolds exhibit higher adsorption potentials than organic matrices. These findings provide strategies for predicting and mitigating VOC emissions from hazardous wastes.
